q: In 1 Corinthians, speaking in tongues without love makes you like what?
quote: but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal.

q: In 1 Corinthians, faith that moves mountains without love makes you what?
quote: and if I have absolute faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.

q: In 1 Corinthians, how does Paul begin describing love?
a: Love is patient, love is kind
why: It does not envy or boast.
quote: Love is patient, love is kind.

q: In 1 Corinthians, which of these does love NOT do?
quote: It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.

q: In 1 Corinthians, what does love keep no account of?
quote: it keeps no account of wrongs.

q: In 1 Corinthians, what does Paul say love never does?
quote: Love never fails.

q: In 1 Corinthians, which three things remain?
quote: And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love

q: In 1 Corinthians, which is the greatest of faith, hope, and love?
quote: but the greatest of these is love.

q: In 1 Corinthians, Paul tells believers they are the body of whom?
why: Each is a member of it.
quote: Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it.

q: In 1 Corinthians, whatever you eat, drink, or do, do it all to the what of God?
why: All of life is for God.
quote: So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.

q: In 1 Corinthians, Paul says to do everything in what?
quote: Do everything in love.

q: In 1 Corinthians, the message of the cross is foolishness to some, but what to us who are saved?
quote: but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.

q: In 1 Corinthians, Paul planted and Apollos watered, but who made it grow?
quote: I planted the seed and Apollos watered it, but God made it grow.

q: In 1 Corinthians, Paul says believers themselves are God's what?
quote: Do you not know that you yourselves are God’s temple

q: In 1 Corinthians, since you were bought at a price, what should you do?
why: Your body is the Spirit's temple.
quote: you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God with your body.

q: In 1 Corinthians, Paul tells believers to run like runners in a race in order to do what?
quote: Run in such a way as to take the prize.

q: In 1 Corinthians, when you are tempted, what will God provide?
quote: But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape

q: In 1 Corinthians, what did Jesus say when He broke the bread?
why: Do this in remembrance of Me.
quote: This is My body, which is for you; do this in remembrance of Me.

q: In 1 Corinthians, Jesus called the cup the new covenant in His what?
quote: This cup is the new covenant in My blood

q: In 1 Corinthians, the body has many parts but forms how many bodies?
quote: And although its parts are many, they all form one body. So it is with Christ.

q: In 1 Corinthians, there are different gifts but the same what?
quote: There are different gifts, but the same Spirit.

q: In 1 Corinthians, when Paul became a man, what did he set aside?
quote: When I became a man, I set aside childish ways.

q: In 1 Corinthians, now we see as in a mirror, but then we shall see how?
quote: Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face.

q: In 1 Corinthians, on which day was Christ raised according to the Scriptures?
quote: that He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures

q: In 1 Corinthians, Paul taunts death, asking, “Where, O Death, is your…”
quote: Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?

q: In 1 Corinthians, what foundation has already been laid?
why: No other foundation can be laid.
quote: For no one can lay a foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.

q: Who is named with Paul at the start of 1 Corinthians?
quote: and our brother Sosthenes

q: In 1 Corinthians, which name did some believers follow besides Paul, Apollos, and Christ?
quote: “I follow Paul,” “I follow Apollos,” “I follow Cephas,” or “I follow Christ.”

q: In 1 Corinthians, to how many brothers at once did the risen Christ appear?
quote: After that, He appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once

q: In 1 Corinthians, what does Paul call the risen Christ?
quote: the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.

q: In 1 Corinthians, at the last trumpet, how fast will we be changed?
a: In the twinkling of an eye
quote: in an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet.

q: In 1 Corinthians, where did Paul say he would stay until Pentecost?
why: A door for work was open.
quote: But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost

q: In 1 Corinthians, what does Paul call Christ who has been sacrificed?
quote: For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.

q: In 1 Corinthians, what has no eye seen and no ear heard?
a: What God prepared for those who love Him
quote: what God has prepared for those who love Him.

q: In 1 Corinthians, love bears, believes, hopes, and endures how many things?
quote: It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
